Surah al-Qadr is Meccan. [Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: Surah "Inna anzalnahu fi laylat al-Qadr" was revealed in Mecca. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/567.] In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

* *

﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree.﴾ It means the Qur'an, by way of allusion to something not mentioned. He sent it down all at once during the Night of Decree from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) to the lowest heaven, and placed it in the House of Glory (Bayt al-'Izzah). Then Jibril, peace be upon him, used to bring it down to him in installments over twenty years [See: Ibn Kathir: 4/530]. Then He made His Prophet wonder, saying: ﴿And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is?﴾ It was called the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr) because it is the night of the determination of affairs and judgments, in which Allah determines the matters of the year concerning His servants and lands until the coming year, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿In it every wise matter is made distinct﴾ [al-Dukhan: 4]. The word is the verbal noun of the expression "qadara Allah al-shay'" in the light form, qadran and qadaran, like "al-nahr" and "al-nahr," and "al-sha'r" and "al-sha'ar"; and "qaddarahu" in the intensive form, taqdiran, with the same meaning. [Qadara in the light form, qadran, has the same meaning.]

It was said to al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: Did not Allah decree the decrees before He created the heavens and the earth? He said: Yes. It was asked: Then what is the meaning of Laylat al-Qadr? He said: The driving of the decrees toward their appointed times, and the execution of the decreed judgment. Al-Azhari said: "Laylat al-Qadr" means the night of greatness and honor, from people's saying: "So-and-so has a qadr (standing) with the ruler," meaning rank and position; and it is said: "qadartu fulanan," meaning I magnified him. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure﴾ [al-An'am: 91] [al-Zumar: 67], meaning they did not magnify Him with His true magnification.

It was also said: because righteous deeds performed in it have great worth (qadr) before Allah, since they are accepted.

They differed about its time. Some said that it existed during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and was then lifted; but the majority of the Companions and scholars hold that it remains until the Day of Resurrection. It was narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Mukanis, a freedman of Mu'awiyah, who said: I said to Abu Hurayrah: They claim that the Night of Decree has been lifted? He said: Whoever says that has lied. I said: Is it in every month that I face? He said: Yes. [Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/570 from 'Abd ibn Humayd.]

Some said: it is a night of the nights of the year, so that if a man attaches the divorce of his wife and the manumission of his slave to the Night of Decree, it does not take effect until a year has passed from the time he swore. This is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: Whoever stands the whole year will attain it. This reached 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, who said: May Allah have mercy on Abu 'Abd al-Rahman. Indeed he knew that it is in the month of Ramadan, but he wanted people not to rely on it alone. [See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/576.]

The majority of scholars hold that it is in the month of Ramadan.

They differed about which night it is. Abu Razin al-'Uqayli said: It is the first night of the month of Ramadan. Al-Hasan said: It is the night of the seventeenth, the night whose morning was the Battle of Badr.

The sound view, and that held by most, is that it is in the last ten nights of Ramadan.

Abu 'Uthman Sa'id ibn Isma'il al-Dabbi informed us, Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jirahi informed us, Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi told us, Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi told us, Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani told us, 'Abdah ibn Sulayman told us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seclude himself in the last ten nights of Ramadan, and he would say: "Seek the Night of Decree in the last ten nights of Ramadan." [Reported by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sawm, chapter on what has come concerning the Night of Decree: 3/504; and al-Bukhari in the virtues of the Night of Decree, chapter on seeking the Night of Decree in the odd nights of the last ten: 4/259; Muslim reported the last clause ("Seek the Night of Decree in the last ten of Ramadan") in al-Siyam, chapter on the virtue of the Night of Decree and encouraging seeking it, no. (1169): 4/828; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/381.]

Abu 'Uthman al-Dabbi informed us, Abu Muhammad al-Jirahi informed us, Abu al-'Abbas al-Mahbubi told us, Abu 'Isa told us, Qutaybah told us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ubayd Allah, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would exert himself in the last ten nights, more than he exerted himself at other times. [Reported by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sawm: 3/509, who said: "This is a gharib hasan sahih hadith." And Muslim in al-I'tikaf, chapter on exerting oneself in the last ten nights of Ramadan, no. (1174): 2/832; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/390.]

'Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il told us, 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah told us, Sufyan told us, from Abu Ya'qub, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: When the last ten nights of Ramadan began, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would tighten his waist-wrapper, stay awake through the night, and wake his family. [Reported by al-Bukhari in the virtues of the Night of Decree, chapter on acts in the last ten nights of Ramadan: 4/269; Muslim in al-I'tikaf, chapter on exerting oneself in the last ten nights of Ramadan, no. (1174): 2/832; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/389.]

They differed as to which night of the ten it is.

'Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il told us, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id told us, Isma'il ibn Ja'far told us, Abu Suhayl ibn Malik told us, from his father, from 'A'ishah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Seek the Night of Decree in the odd nights of the last ten nights of Ramadan." [Reported by al-Bukhari in the virtues of the Night of Decree, chapter on seeking the Night of Decree in the odd nights of the last ten: 4/259; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/381-382.]

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazin informed us, Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us, 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim [in A: Hisham, and the correct reading is what we have set down, as in al-Tahdhib] ibn Hayyan told us, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan told us, 'Uyaynah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman told us, my father told me, saying: I mentioned the Night of Decree in the presence of Abu Bakrah, and he said: I am not seeking it except in the last ten nights, because of something I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Seek it in the last ten nights: on the ninth remaining, or the seventh remaining, or the fifth remaining, or the third remaining, or the last night." [Reported by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sawm, chapter on what has come concerning the Night of Decree: 3/507-508, who said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith"; Ibn Hibban, page (231) of Mawarid al-Dhaman; Ibn Khuzaymah: 3/324; al-Hakim authenticated it: 1/438, and al-Dhahabi agreed; al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman: 7/280; Imam Ahmad: 5/36; al-Tayalisi in his Musnad, page (118), no. (881); and Ibn Abi Shaybah: 3/76. Al-Albani authenticated it in his commentary on al-Mishkat, no. (2092), and in Sahih al-Jami', no. (1243). See also the hadiths on specifying the Night of Decree in detail in Ibn Hajar al-Haytami's Ithaf Ahl al-Islam bi-Khususiyat al-Siyam, page (166) and following.] Abu Bakrah, when Ramadan came, would pray as he prayed during the rest of the year; but when the last ten [in B: "al-Awakhir"] came, he would exert himself.

'Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il told us, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Khalid ibn al-Harith told me, Humayd told us, Anas ibn Malik told us, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) went out to inform us of the Night of Decree, but two men among the Muslims quarreled, and he said: "I went out to inform you of the Night of Decree, but so-and-so and so-and-so quarreled, and it was lifted. Perhaps it is better for you. So seek it on the ninth, the seventh, and the fifth." [Reported by al-Bukhari in the virtues of the Night of Decree, chapter: the lifting of knowledge of the Night of Decree because people quarreled: 4/267; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/380.]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Nafi', from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, that some men among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) were shown the Night of Decree in a dream in the last seven nights of Ramadan. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I see that your dreams agree in the last seven nights, so whoever seeks it, let him seek it in the last seven nights." [Reported by Imam Malik in al-Muwatta', kitab al-i'tikaf, chapter on what has come concerning the Night of Decree: 1/320; al-Bukhari in the virtues of the Night of Decree, chapter on seeking the Night of Decree in the last seven nights: 4/256; Muslim in al-Siyam, chapter on the virtue of the Night of Decree and encouraging seeking it, no. (1165): 2/822-823; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/381.] It is also narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that it is the night of the twenty-first.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Had, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to seclude himself in the middle ten nights of Ramadan. One year he secluded himself until the night of the twenty-first, which was the night from whose morning he would come out of his seclusion. He said: "Whoever was going to seclude himself with me, let him seclude himself in the last ten nights. I saw this night and then I was made to forget it. I saw myself prostrating on its morning in water and mud. So seek it in the last ten nights, and seek it in every odd night." [Reported by Imam Malik in al-I'tikaf, chapter on what has come concerning the Night of Decree: 1/319; al-Bukhari in al-I'tikaf, chapter on seclusion in the last ten nights: 4/271; Muslim in al-Siyam, chapter on the virtue of the Night of Decree and encouraging seeking it, no. (1167): 2/825; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/383-384.]

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: The sky rained that night, and the mosque was roofed with palm branches, so the mosque leaked. Abu Sa'id said: My eyes saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) leave, and on his forehead and nose were traces of water and mud, from the morning of the twenty-first.

Some said: it is the night of the twenty-third.

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 97, verses 1–2 (part 2 of 2):

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: Abu Mansur al-Samʿani informed us, who said: Abu Jaʿfar al-Rayyani related to us, who said: Humayd ibn Zanjuwayh related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Himsi related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Unays related to me, from his father, that he said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "I am in a desert called al-Wat'ah, and by the praise of Allah I lead them in prayer. So command me to a night of this month, that I may come down to the mosque and pray it therein." He said: "Come down on the night of the twenty-third and pray it therein. And if you wish to complete the last of the month, then do so. And if you wish, then refrain." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the Book of Prayer, chapter on the Night of Qadr: 2/110; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 4/310, and in Shuʿab al-Iman: 7/276; al-Tahawi in Sharh Maʿani al-Athar: 3/88; and ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 4/251. Malik narrated it as mursal (disconnected): 1/320, and it was connected by Muslim and others as previously mentioned. Al-Mundhiri said: "Its chain includes Muhammad ibn Ishaq, whose case has been discussed earlier. Muslim in his Sahih, in the Book of Fasting, number (1168), narrated from the hadith of Busr ibn Saʿid, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Unays, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I was shown the Night of Qadr and then I was made to forget it, and I saw myself prostrating in water and mud.' He said: 'It rained on the night of the twenty-third, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led us in prayer; when he finished, the traces of water and mud were on his forehead and nose.'" As for Ibn Ishaq, his tadlis (concealment) does not harm, as it is not among what undermines uprightness; the scholar al-Lakhnawi wrote at length in refuting his criticism and concluded with his authentication in his book "Imam al-Kalam fima yata'allaq bil-Qira'a Khalf al-Imam," pages (280–290). In sum, it is hasan (good), though it has been disputed, and it is of good narration as al-Mundhiri said. See Majma' al-Zawa'id: 3/178.]]. He said: So when he prayed the afternoon prayer, he would enter the mosque and not leave except for a need, until he prayed the dawn prayer; and when he had prayed the dawn prayer, his mount would be at the door of the mosque.

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: Abu Mansur al-Samʿani informed us, who said: Abu Jaʿfar al-Rayyani related to us, who said: Humayd ibn Zanjuwayh related to us, who said: Yaʿla ibn ʿUbayd related to us, who said: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: We discussed the Night of Qadr, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How many days of the month have passed?" We said: "Twenty-two [[Omitted in "a"]] and seven remain." ["Twenty-two have passed and seven remain," he said.] [[Omitted in "a"]] "Seek it tonight. The month is twenty-nine [days]." [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf: 3/84, and through him by Ibn Majah in the Book of Fasting, chapter on "The month is twenty-nine," number (1656): 1/530. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id: "Its chain is sahih according to the condition of Muslim," and Shaykh Ahmad Shakir in his commentary on the Musnad added that it is according to the condition of al-Bukhari. Ibn Hibban authenticated it, page (230) of Mawarid al-Zam'an. It was also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan, 4/310, and by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 2/251 with a sahih chain, and with the commentary of Shaykh Ahmad Shakir: 13/156. The author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/386.]]

Some people said: It is the night of the twenty-seventh, and this is the view of ʿAli, Ubayy and ʿAʾisha:

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: Abu Mansur al-Samʿani informed us, who said: Abu Jaʿfar al-Rayyani related to us, who said: Humayd ibn Zanjuwayh related to us, who said: Yaʿla ibn ʿUbayd related to us, who said: Sufyan related to us, from ʿAsim, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: I said to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "O Abu al-Mundhir, inform us about the Night of Qadr, for Ibn Umm ʿAbd says: 'Whoever stands (in prayer) the whole year will attain it.'" He said: "May Allah have mercy on Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman. Indeed he knows that it is in Ramadan, but he disliked to inform you lest you rely on it. By Him who sent down the Qur'an upon Muhammad (ﷺ), it is the night of the twenty-seventh." We said: "O Abu al-Mundhir, how did you know this?" He said: "By the sign which the Prophet (ﷺ) informed us of, and we memorized and counted it. It is, by Allah, not forgotten." He said: We said to Zirr: "What is the sign?" He said: "The sun rises like a basin, without rays." [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Fasting, chapter on the virtue of the Night of Qadr and encouragement to seek it, number (762): 2/828; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/387.]]

Among its signs is what is narrated from al-Hasan, raised (to the Prophet ﷺ): that it is a night [[i.e., illuminated, clear; al-Nihayah: 1/151.]] serene, neither hot nor cold, and the sun rises on its morning without rays. [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf from al-Hasan as mursal: 3/514, and ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 4/252–253. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath, 4/260: "Signs have been reported for the Night of Qadr, most of which do not appear until after it has passed. Among them, in Sahih Muslim from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb (the previous hadith); and in a narration of Ahmad: 'like a basin,' and similar in Ahmad from Abu ʿAwn from Ibn Masʿud, adding: 'clear'; and from Ibn ʿAbbas similarly; and in Ibn Khuzaymah from his hadith, raised: 'The Night of Qadr is clear, illuminated, pure, neither hot nor cold...'"]]

In general: Allah concealed this night from this Ummah so that they would strive in worship during the nights of Ramadan, hoping to attain it, just as He concealed the hour of answered supplication on Friday, and concealed the middle prayer among the five prayers, and His Greatest Name among the names, and His pleasure in acts of obedience so that they would eagerly pursue all of them, and His wrath in acts of disobedience so that they would refrain from all of them, and He concealed the establishment of the Hour so that they would strive in acts of obedience, out of fear of its occurrence.

I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Seek it in the last ten nights: on the ninth remaining, or the seventh remaining, or the fifth remaining, or the third remaining, or the last night." [Reported by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sawm, chapter on what has come concerning the Night of Decree: 3/507-508, who said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith"; Ibn Hibban, page (231) of Mawarid al-Dhaman; Ibn Khuzaymah: 3/324; al-Hakim authenticated it: 1/438, and al-Dhahabi agreed; al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman: 7/280; Imam Ahmad: 5/36; al-Tayalisi in his Musnad, page (118), no. (881); and Ibn Abi Shaybah: 3/76. Al-Albani authenticated it in his commentary on al-Mishkat, no. (2092), and in Sahih al-Jami', no. (1243). See also the hadiths on specifying the Night of Decree in detail in Ibn Hajar al-Haytami's Ithaf Ahl al-Islam bi-Khususiyat al-Siyam, page (166) and following.] Abu Bakrah, when Ramadan came, would pray as he prayed during the rest of the year; but when the last ten [in B: "al-Awakhir"] came, he would exert himself.

'Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il told us, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Khalid ibn al-Harith told me, Humayd told us, Anas ibn Malik told us, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) went out to inform us of the Night of Decree, but two men among the Muslims quarreled, and he said: "I went out to inform you of the Night of Decree, but so-and-so and so-and-so quarreled, and it was lifted. Perhaps it is better for you. So seek it on the ninth, the seventh, and the fifth." [Reported by al-Bukhari in the virtues of the Night of Decree, chapter: the lifting of knowledge of the Night of Decree because people quarreled: 4/267; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/380.]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Nafi', from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, that some men among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) were shown the Night of Decree in a dream in the last seven nights of Ramadan. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I see that your dreams agree in the last seven nights, so whoever seeks it, let him seek it in the last seven nights." [Reported by Imam Malik in al-Muwatta', kitab al-i'tikaf, chapter on what has come concerning the Night of Decree: 1/320; al-Bukhari in the virtues of the Night of Decree, chapter on seeking the Night of Decree in the last seven nights: 4/256; Muslim in al-Siyam, chapter on the virtue of the Night of Decree and encouraging seeking it, no. (1165): 2/822-823; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/381.] It is also narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that it is the night of the twenty-first.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Had, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to seclude himself in the middle ten nights of Ramadan. One year he secluded himself until the night of the twenty-first, which was the night from whose morning he would come out of his seclusion. He said: "Whoever was going to seclude himself with me, let him seclude himself in the last ten nights. I saw this night and then I was made to forget it. I saw myself prostrating on its morning in water and mud. So seek it in the last ten nights, and seek it in every odd night." [Reported by Imam Malik in al-I'tikaf, chapter on what has come concerning the Night of Decree: 1/319; al-Bukhari in al-I'tikaf, chapter on seclusion in the last ten nights: 4/271; Muslim in al-Siyam, chapter on the virtue of the Night of Decree and encouraging seeking it, no. (1167): 2/825; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/383-384.]

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: The sky rained that night, and the mosque was roofed with palm branches, so the mosque leaked. Abu Sa'id said: My eyes saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) leave, and on his forehead and nose were traces of water and mud, from the morning of the twenty-first.

Some said: it is the night of the twenty-third.

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 97, verses 1–2 (part 2 of 2):

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: Abu Mansur al-Samʿani informed us, who said: Abu Jaʿfar al-Rayyani related to us, who said: Humayd ibn Zanjuwayh related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Himsi related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Unays related to me, from his father, that he said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "I am in a desert called al-Wat'ah, and by the praise of Allah I lead them in prayer. So command me to a night of this month, that I may come down to the mosque and pray it therein." He said: "Come down on the night of the twenty-third and pray it therein. And if you wish to complete the last of the month, then do so. And if you wish, then refrain." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the Book of Prayer, chapter on the Night of Qadr: 2/110; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 4/310, and in Shuʿab al-Iman: 7/276; al-Tahawi in Sharh Maʿani al-Athar: 3/88; and ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 4/251. Malik narrated it as mursal (disconnected): 1/320, and it was connected by Muslim and others as previously mentioned. Al-Mundhiri said: "Its chain includes Muhammad ibn Ishaq, whose case has been discussed earlier. Muslim in his Sahih, in the Book of Fasting, number (1168), narrated from the hadith of Busr ibn Saʿid, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Unays, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I was shown the Night of Qadr and then I was made to forget it, and I saw myself prostrating in water and mud.' He said: 'It rained on the night of the twenty-third, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led us in prayer; when he finished, the traces of water and mud were on his forehead and nose.'" As for Ibn Ishaq, his tadlis (concealment) does not harm, as it is not among what undermines uprightness; the scholar al-Lakhnawi wrote at length in refuting his criticism and concluded with his authentication in his book "Imam al-Kalam fima yata'allaq bil-Qira'a Khalf al-Imam," pages (280–290). In sum, it is hasan (good), though it has been disputed, and it is of good narration as al-Mundhiri said. See Majma' al-Zawa'id: 3/178.]]. He said: So when he prayed the afternoon prayer, he would enter the mosque and not leave except for a need, until he prayed the dawn prayer; and when he had prayed the dawn prayer, his mount would be at the door of the mosque.

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: Abu Mansur al-Samʿani informed us, who said: Abu Jaʿfar al-Rayyani related to us, who said: Humayd ibn Zanjuwayh related to us, who said: Yaʿla ibn ʿUbayd related to us, who said: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: We discussed the Night of Qadr, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How many days of the month have passed?" We said: "Twenty-two [[Omitted in "a"]] and seven remain." ["Twenty-two have passed and seven remain," he said.] [[Omitted in "a"]] "Seek it tonight. The month is twenty-nine [days]." [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf: 3/84, and through him by Ibn Majah in the Book of Fasting, chapter on "The month is twenty-nine," number (1656): 1/530. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id: "Its chain is sahih according to the condition of Muslim," and Shaykh Ahmad Shakir in his commentary on the Musnad added that it is according to the condition of al-Bukhari. Ibn Hibban authenticated it, page (230) of Mawarid al-Zam'an. It was also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan, 4/310, and by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 2/251 with a sahih chain, and with the commentary of Shaykh Ahmad Shakir: 13/156. The author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/386.]]

Some people said: It is the night of the twenty-seventh, and this is the view of ʿAli, Ubayy and ʿAʾisha:

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: Abu Mansur al-Samʿani informed us, who said: Abu Jaʿfar al-Rayyani related to us, who said: Humayd ibn Zanjuwayh related to us, who said: Yaʿla ibn ʿUbayd related to us, who said: Sufyan related to us, from ʿAsim, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: I said to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "O Abu al-Mundhir, inform us about the Night of Qadr, for Ibn Umm ʿAbd says: 'Whoever stands (in prayer) the whole year will attain it.'" He said: "May Allah have mercy on Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman. Indeed he knows that it is in Ramadan, but he disliked to inform you lest you rely on it. By Him who sent down the Qur'an upon Muhammad (ﷺ), it is the night of the twenty-seventh." We said: "O Abu al-Mundhir, how did you know this?" He said: "By the sign which the Prophet (ﷺ) informed us of, and we memorized and counted it. It is, by Allah, not forgotten." He said: We said to Zirr: "What is the sign?" He said: "The sun rises like a basin, without rays." [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Fasting, chapter on the virtue of the Night of Qadr and encouragement to seek it, number (762): 2/828; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/387.]]

Among its signs is what is narrated from al-Hasan, raised (to the Prophet ﷺ): that it is a night [[i.e., illuminated, clear; al-Nihayah: 1/151.]] serene, neither hot nor cold, and the sun rises on its morning without rays. [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf from al-Hasan as mursal: 3/514, and ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 4/252–253. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath, 4/260: "Signs have been reported for the Night of Qadr, most of which do not appear until after it has passed. Among them, in Sahih Muslim from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb (the previous hadith); and in a narration of Ahmad: 'like a basin,' and similar in Ahmad from Abu ʿAwn from Ibn Masʿud, adding: 'clear'; and from Ibn ʿAbbas similarly; and in Ibn Khuzaymah from his hadith, raised: 'The Night of Qadr is clear, illuminated, pure, neither hot nor cold...'"]]

In general: Allah concealed this night from this Ummah so that they would strive in worship during the nights of Ramadan, hoping to attain it, just as He concealed the hour of answered supplication on Friday, and concealed the middle prayer among the five prayers, and His Greatest Name among the names, and His pleasure in acts of obedience so that they would eagerly pursue all of them, and His wrath in acts of disobedience so that they would refrain from all of them, and He concealed the establishment of the Hour so that they would strive in acts of obedience, out of fear of its occurrence.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 97, verse 3:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾. Ata' related from Ibn 'Abbas: It was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that a man from the Children of Israel bore weapons upon his shoulder in the way of Allah for a thousand months. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was amazed at this and wished such for his community. He said: "O Lord, You have made my community the shortest of the nations in lifespan and the least in deeds." So Allah gave him the Night of Decree, and He said: ﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾, the night in which the Israelite bore weapons in the way of Allah, for you and your community until the Day of Resurrection. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 3/289-290, and al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 533, both from Mujahid. It was also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 4/306, who said: "This is mursal," and he alluded to it in Shu'ab al-Iman 7/265. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir from the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim from Mujahid that the Prophet ﷺ mentioned a man from the Children of Israel... It is munqati' (disconnected), and in its chain is Muslim ibn Khalid al-Zanji, a truthful narrator who has errors.]]

The exegetes said: "The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months" means: a righteous deed performed in the Night of Decree is better than the deeds of a thousand months in which there is no Night of Decree.

Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Karim ibn Hawazin al-Qushayri related to us by dictation: Abu Nu'aym al-Isfara'ini related to us: Abu 'Awana informed us: Abu Isma'il related to us: al-Humaydi related to us: Sufyan related to us: al-Zuhri related to us: Abu Salama informed me, from Abu Hurayra, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever stands in prayer on the Night of Decree out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Tarawih, chapter on the virtue of one who stands in prayer in Ramadan: 4/250, and Muslim in Salat al-Musafirin, chapter on encouraging the standing in prayer in Ramadan, no. (760): 1/524.]]

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: Whoever attends the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers in congregation has taken his share of the Night of Decree. [[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/582.]]

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us: Abu Bakr ibn 'Abdus al-Muzakki informed us: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us: al-Hasan ibn Mukram related to us: Yazid ibn Harun related to us: Kahmas informed us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Buraydah, that 'A'isha said to the Prophet ﷺ: "If I encounter the Night of Decree, what should I say?" He said: "Say: O Allah, You are Pardoning and You love pardon, so pardon me." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Da'awat: 9/495, who said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith," and al-Nasa'i in al-Tafsir: 2/538, and in 'Amal al-Yawm wa al-Layla p. 499, and from his route Ibn al-Sunni in 'Amal al-Yawm wa al-Layla p. 359; Ibn Majah no. (3850): 2/1265; al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman: 7/299; Imam Ahmad: 6/171, 182, 183; al-Hakim: 2/530, who declared it sahih according to the conditions of al-Shaykhayn and al-Dhahabi agreed; and Muhammad ibn Nasr in Qiyam al-Layl and Qiyam Ramadan p. 239, from the Mukhtasar of al-Maqrizi. It was declared sahih by al-Nawawi in al-Adhkar. See also: al-Futuhat al-Rabbaniyya 'ala al-Adhkar al-Nawawiyya by Ibn 'Allan: 4/346.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 97, verses 4–5:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein﴾ — meaning Jibril (peace be upon him) along with them — ﴿therein﴾, i.e., during the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr), ﴿by the permission of their Lord, with every command﴾, i.e., with every command of good and blessing, like His saying: "They guard him by the command of Allah" [al-Ra'd: 11], i.e., by the command of Allah.

﴿Peace﴾ — ʿAṭāʾ said: it means peace upon the friends of Allah and the people of His obedience. Al-Sha'bi said: it is the greeting of the angels on the Night of Decree to the people of the mosques, from sunset until the break of dawn. [[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi from him in Shu'ab al-Iman: 7/299, its narrators are trustworthy; and al-Qurtubi mentioned it from him: 20/134.]]

Al-Kalbi said: the angels descend during it, and whenever they meet a believing man or believing woman, they greet them on behalf of their Lord, until the break of dawn.

It was also said: the statement is complete at His saying, "by the permission of their Lord, with every command," and then He begins, saying, "Peace is it," i.e., the Night of Decree is peace and entirely good, with no evil in it.

Al-Dahhak said: Allah does not decree or determine in that night except safety.

Mujahid said: it means that the Night of Decree is [safe] [[Omitted from manuscript "a".]]; Satan cannot do any harm in it nor cause any injury. [[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman: 7/299. Also mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/569–570, attributing it to Sa'id ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Muhammad ibn Nasr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi.]]

﴿Until the rising of the dawn﴾ — i.e., until the rising of the dawn. Al-Kisa'i read "maṭli'" with a kasra on the lam, while the others read it with a fatha, and this is the preferred reading, in the sense of the act of rising, as a verbal noun. It is said: "ṭalaʿa al-fajru ṭulūʿan wa maṭlaʿan" (the dawn rose). The kasra form denotes the place of rising.
